q: 1. In a closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is ...............
explain: For a closed traverse, the algebraic sum of the deflection angles must equal 360°.

q: 2. Under ordinary conditions, the precision of a theodolite traverse is affected by
explain: Under normal conditions, angular measurements with a theodolite are quite precise and accidental errors in angle are small; it is the systematic (cumulative) errors in the linear (chain/tape) measurements that mainly govern the overall precision of the traverse.

q: 3. The most reliable method of plotting a theodolite traverse is
options: by consecutive co-ordinates of each station
by independent co-ordinates of each station
by plotting included angles and scaling off each traverse leg
by the tangent method of plotting
explain: Plotting by independent (total) co-ordinates of each station, computed from the origin, avoids the accumulation of plotting errors that occurs when each point is plotted relative to the previous one (consecutive co-ordinates), making it the most reliable method.

q: 4. The operation of making the algebraic sum of latitudes and departures of a closed traverse, each equal to zero, is known
explain: Adjusting all the latitudes and departures of a closed traverse so that their algebraic sums each become zero (removing the closing error) is called balancing the traverse.

q: 5. A well conditioned triangle has no angle less than ...............
explain: A triangle is well-conditioned if its angles are between 30° and 120° to ensure accurate intersection points.

q: 6. In a closed traverse
options: the difference between fore bearing & back bearing should be 90°
the sum of included angles should be (2N-4) right angle, where N is the number of sides
the sum of inclined angles should be (2N-1), where N is the number of sides
explain: The geometric property of a closed polygon dictates that the sum of the interior angles is given by the formula (2N - 4) x 90 degrees.

q: 7. In a theodolite the line of collimation is
options: parallel to axes of plate level
explain: For correct instrument geometry, the line of collimation of a theodolite telescope must be exactly perpendicular to the trunnion (horizontal) axis about which the telescope rotates.

q: 8. A 15 cm theodolite means
options: length of the telescope is 15 cm
diameter of lower plate is 15 cm
radius of upper plate is 15 cm.
explain: The size of a theodolite is designated by the diameter of its lower (graduated horizontal) plate; thus a '15 cm theodolite' has a lower plate 15 cm in diameter.

q: 9. left swing is not much favoured in theodolite survey because
options: most of the surveyors are accustomed to right hand
it is inconvenient to turn the telescope anti-clockwise
vertical scale comes to an inconvenient position to be read.
explain: Since the horizontal circle of a theodolite is graduated to increase in the clockwise direction, swinging the telescope anti-clockwise (left swing) causes the readings to decrease, which is inconvenient for booking and computation.

q: 10. The projection of a traverse line on a line parallel to the meridian is known as
explain: Latitude is the projection of a line on the North-South axis (parallel to the meridian).

q: 11. In a closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is
explain: For a closed traverse, the algebraic sum of all the deflection angles (right deflections positive, left negative) is always equal to 360 degrees.

q: 12. When internal angles are to be subtended by a theodolite survey for closed traverse
options: exterior angles are measured when the traverse goes anti-clockwise.
explain: To measure the internal (interior) angles of a closed traverse correctly and consistently, the traverse should be run in the counter-clockwise direction.

q: 13. For which of the following permanent adjustments of theodolite, the spire test is used?
options: adjustment of altitude bubble and vertical index frame
explain: The spire test is used to make the horizontal axis perpendicular to the vertical axis.

q: 14. The angular error of closure or summation error should not exceed
options: 3√N where N is number of stations or sides.
explain: The standard permissible angular closure error in compass surveying is typically defined as 15' multiplied by the square root of the number of stations.

q: 15. If 'n' is the number of sides, then the total sum of interior angles of a closed traverse should be
explain: The sum of interior angles of a closed polygon of n sides is given by the standard geometric formula (2n - 4) x 90 degrees.

q: 16. In order to measure a horizontal angle more accurately than a vernier, a
options: method of deflection angles is used
method of double observations is used
explain: The method of repetition involves measuring the same angle multiple times and dividing the total by the number of repetitions, which reduces the error caused by the least count of the vernier.

q: 17. According to Bowditch Rule, the correction to latitude (or departure) of any side is equal to
options: Length of the side / Perimeter of traverse
Perimeter of traverse / Length of the side
Total error in latitude / Perimeter of traverse
Total error in latitude x Length of that side / Perimeter of traverse
explain: Bowditch's rule states that the correction to the latitude (or departure) of a side is proportional to the length of that side: Correction = Total error in latitude x (Length of that side / Perimeter of traverse).

q: 18. The theodolite is an instrument used for measuring very accurately .............
explain: The primary function of a theodolite is the precise measurement of both horizontal and vertical angles.

q: 19. The process of turning the telescope of a theodolite over its supporting axis through 180° in a vertical plane, is called .............
explain: Transiting, plunging, and reversing are synonymous terms for rotating the telescope 180° around its horizontal (trunnion) axis.

q: 20. In a theodolite the line of collimation is .............
options: parallel to axis of plate levels
explain: For a properly adjusted theodolite, the line of collimation (the optical axis) must be perpendicular to the horizontal (trunnion) axis.

q: 21. The process of turning the telescope about the horizontal axis in a vertical plane by a complete revolution is known as
explain: All three terms—reversing, transiting, and plunging—describe the act of flipping the telescope over its horizontal axis.

q: 22. Which among the following is a procedure for computation of traverse area?
options: Calculation and adjustment of latitudes and departures
explain: Computing the area of a closed traverse requires first calculating and adjusting (balancing) the latitudes and departures of all its sides, from which co-ordinates and area are then derived.

q: 23. For adjusting the traverse, which of the following methods can be used?
explain: Bowditch's method (rule) is the standard method used specifically for adjusting/balancing the latitudes and departures of a closed traverse.

q: 24. Which of the following is the accurate method for plotting traverse area?
explain: As with plotting theodolite traverses generally (Q71), the co-ordinate method (plotting each station by its independent co-ordinates) is the most accurate way to plot a traverse area.

q: 25. The projection of a line on a plane parallel to meridian is known as
explain: Latitude is the orthographic projection of a line onto the North-South meridian (L cos θ).

q: 26. When the latitudes and departures are so adjusted that the algebraic sum of the latitudes and departures are equal to zero, the operation is called .............
explain: Balancing the traverse is the process of adjusting observed latitudes and departures to eliminate the closing error so that the traverse forms a mathematically closed figure.

q: 27. In a theodolite the line passing through the intersection of the horizontal and vertical cross hairs and optical centre of the object glass and its continuation is known as
explain: The line of collimation is the specific imaginary line defined by the crosshairs and the optical center of the objective lens.

q: 28. The fundamental lines of transit are
options: horizontal axis and line of collimation
axes of plate levels and bubble line of telescope level
explain: The geometry of a theodolite is based on several axes (Vertical, Horizontal, Collimation, Bubble) being in specific relationships (perpendicular or parallel).

q: 29. A deflection angle in a traverse is equal to the .............
options: difference between the included angle and 180°
difference between 360° and the included angle and 180°
sum of the included angel and 180°
explain: In any traverse, the deflection angle at a station is 180° minus the internal included angle (or included angle - 180° for external).

q: 30. Pantagraph is used for .............
explain: A pantagraph is a mechanical linkage based on parallelograms used to copy a plan at a different scale (reduction or enlargement).

q: 31. If the included angle is greater than 180°, the deflection angle is
explain: An included angle > 180° results in a deflection to the right of the forward-extended line.

q: 32. If the included angle is less than 180°, the deflection angle is
explain: An included angle < 180° results in a deflection to the left (negative) of the forward-extended line.

q: 33. Total latitude of a point is positive if it lies .............
explain: By convention in surveying, Northings (Latitude North) are considered positive and Southings are negative.

q: 34. The altitude of a traverse leg is obtained by multiplying its length by .............
explain: Latitude (often referred to here as altitude in context of projection) = L cos θ, where L is the length and θ is the reduced bearing.

q: 35. The operation of making the algebraic sum of latitudes and departures of a closed traverse, each equal to zero, is known .............
explain: This describes the fundamental definition of balancing a traverse to ensure closure.

q: 36. Bowditch rule is applied to
options: an open traverse for graphical adjustment
determine the effect of local attraction
a closed traverse for adjustment of closing error
explain: Bowditch's rule is a standard method for balancing a closed traverse when linear and angular measurements are of equal precision.

q: 37. Direction of closing error in given by
explain: The direction (bearing) θ of the closing error is given by tan θ = (Sum of Departures / Sum of Latitudes).

q: 38. The angular and linear measurement of the part of the traverse can be checked by
explain: Cut-off lines and observations to distant known objects are common ways to verify accuracy within a large traverse.

q: 39. The maximum number of omitted measurements that can be calculated from latitudes and departures of a closed traverse is
explain: Since there are two independent equations (ΣL=0 and ΣD=0), you can solve for a maximum of two unknowns (e.g., one length and one bearing).

q: 40. The direct angles may have any value between
explain: Direct angles (angles to the right) are measured clockwise from the back station to the forward station and can range anywhere from 0° to 360°.

q: 41. For removing the parallax
options: image brought in plane of cross-hairs...
explain: Parallax is eliminated by first focusing the eyepiece for the observer's eye and then focusing the objective to ensure the image falls exactly on the plane of the cross-hairs.

q: 42. The capacity of a telescope of producing a sharp image is called its
explain: Definition (or resolving power) refers to the clarity and sharpness of the image produced by the telescope's lenses.

q: 43. For a closed traverse the omitted measurements may be calculated .............
options: length or bearing of adjacent side
explain: In a closed traverse, if $\sum Latitude = 0$ and $\sum Departure = 0$, you can solve for up to two unknown quantities (like one length and one bearing, or two lengths).

q: 44. The length of a traverse line (L) may be obtained by .............
explain: All three formulas are mathematically valid based on the geometry of coordinates and bearings ($Lat = L \cos \theta$, $Dep = L \sin \theta$).

q: 45. While rotating the theodolite in the horizontal plane, the bubble of the bubble tube takes up the same position in its tube, it indicates .............
options: the line of collimation is perpendicular to vertical axis
explain: If the bubble remains centered throughout a 360-degree rotation, it confirms the vertical axis of the instrument is truly vertical.

q: 46. Centering error of a theodolite produces an error .............
options: which does not vary with the direction or pointing
which varies with the direction of pointing and inversely with the length of sight
explain: The effect of centering error is more significant on short sights than on long sights.

q: 47. Which of the following errors can be eliminated by taking mean of both face observations?
options: errors due to eccentricity of verniers
errors due to imperfect adjustments of plate levels
errors due to line of collimation not being perpendicular to horizontal axis
explain: Taking the average of Face Left and Face Right readings eliminates instrumental errors such as the horizontal axis not being perpendicular to the vertical axis.
